# JobCtrl v0.4.1

JobCtrl v0.4.1 improves job imports, profile and resume handling, Discovery, and application recovery. Compatible installed and source runtimes share a workspace and can upgrade supported databases automatically.

## Workspace and updates

- Compatible installed apps and Git checkouts use the same local workspace, profile, resume, and Temporal history. Source startup upgrades supported older databases automatically when it can verify process ownership, after stopping the owned processes and taking a paired application and history backup.
- Concurrent credential updates are serialized so an earlier failed save cannot undo a newer one.
- Automatic cleanup preserves releases referenced by paired backups in registered workspaces and stops when those references cannot be verified.
- This release moves supported workspaces from schema 14 to schema 15. When process ownership can be verified, its authenticated installer backs up the current application database and Temporal history together before migration. It preserves the live workspace and resumes forward after an interrupted upgrade rather than restoring an older snapshot over later changes.
- **Known upgrade limitation:** v0.3.1 installations that have run normally lack complete child-process ownership records. The new installer refuses their upgrade because it cannot verify that all earlier processes stopped. It preserves the existing workspace and installation records. Stay on v0.3.1 until a compatible upgrade is available. In particular, upgrading the Homebrew formula makes its `jobctrl` command attempt this blocked transition, so that command cannot start the existing workspace. There is currently no documented self-service recovery for that case; see [update and recovery instructions](https://jobctrl.dev/user/getting-started#update-roll-back-or-remove-jobctrl).
- After the migration, older releases that cannot read schema 15 cannot open the workspace. Rollback across this protocol and schema change is unavailable. Keep the existing installation metadata and workspace; see [update and recovery instructions](https://jobctrl.dev/user/getting-started#update-roll-back-or-remove-jobctrl).
- A compatible installed update uses the new authenticated installer for this protocol transition. Older schemas and unverified legacy source history have additional limitations; see [Local Development](https://jobctrl.dev/local-development#schema-migrations-and-source-updates). Do not delete the registry or replace either database to bypass a refusal.

## Job search and materials

- Continue adding job posting URLs while earlier imports run in the background, and follow each import's progress.
- Resume generation keeps applicable accomplishments within the saved per-role limits, respects selected optional skills, and preserves saved profile identities and resume upload recovery.
- Cover letters are opt-in. Material reviews preserve accepted versions and their provenance when a refresh fails or a newer review is saved.
- Discovery and preparation recover more reliably from canceled runs, source limits, unavailable postings, provider outages, and interrupted work. Job and pipeline views expose progress and failures more accurately.
- Pipeline retries show when a stage was reset without being dispatched, and stale-score recovery points to the supported command. The demo reflects the same retry states.
- The worker limits abandoned activity generations after cancellations, and Pipeline Operations shows whether stage and control work can be admitted.
- Job deletion and application cleanup are fenced against stale or conflicting work. Apply retains explicit review and submission controls.
- Source-checkout Apply recognizes its authenticated source fleet context instead of rejecting valid work. That context does not replace per-attempt execution custody.
- Outcome and reflection drafts and retries remain scoped to their tenant and job, including when switching between sections.
- Contact research limits slow or oversized public-source responses and preserves accepted proposals when overlapping attempts fail.

## Requirements

The signed installer and Homebrew package support Apple-silicon macOS 15 or later. Source development has separate toolchain requirements. Scoring, generation, and other model-backed work require a configured provider and available budget. Review generated materials and application actions before use; the browser extension does not submit applications.
